title: People adopted false facts from confident AI tutors
summary: In a study with 32 volunteers, participants selected an assistant’s planted false answer for about 60% of quiz items assigned false information, compared with 11% of items assigned correct information. Mean scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10 between fully accurate and fully falsified GPT-5-mini briefings.
organization: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Indian Institute of Science

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 trial design §§3.1–3.7, Table 3, §4.2 and ethics statement

evidence.tested: The counterbalanced study used five briefing reliability levels and 104 completed quizzes, with independently randomized topic order and corrective debriefing.
evidence.unknown: This was a small study with one underlying model, deliberately confident responses, and immediate quizzes. Retention over longer periods and responses to other assistants were not assessed. Participants could continue consulting the same assistant during each quiz. The measured choices do not establish unaided memory retention or durable internalized beliefs.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5-mini chat assistants explained science topics from briefings containing controlled levels of plausible false claims.
